findings: The general-star predicate requires actual center-to-leaf edges, exact selected branch size and disjointness; it does not inadvertently require induced claws. Extra host edges among leaves are retained in the full quotient semantics.

The full minor model constructs connectivity by two actual star walks, proves branch disjointness against the original residual set, and retains all host vertices and crossing adjacencies. The boundedness proof correctly requires k>=1 for residual singleton branches.

Covered cardinality is exactly k times the number of selected centers. The quotient identity uses the actual center/residual index type and proves the subtraction is safe from covered cardinality<=|V|.

The empty-family quotient has an explicit injective edge-preserving map from the original host. This discharges its actual edge-loss admissibility for arbitrary real D and q, with zero covered vertices.

Finite maximum ranges over all finite center sets and leaf functions, using the literal quotient-loss and covered-small-vertex predicates. The comparison is exact center count. No positive coverage, extension oracle or residual-degree theorem is hidden in the conclusion.
